data.reason: WAN NIC vtnet0 is hung: repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" in dmesg, 48211 Tx errors on vtnet0, ARP to upstream gateway 198.51.100.1 incomplete, and sends fail with ENOBUFS. Four WAN interface reloads during this outage (rc=0) did not restore connectivity, so an interface reload does not clear the stuck driver; a full reboot is needed to reset the NIC. The modem itself reports OPERATIONAL, so modem_reboot would not help, and the reload cap (12/24h) has already been reached.

data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface vtnet0 is stuck: dmesg shows repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link down/up cycles, 48k Tx errors accumulated, and packets cannot leave the box (ENOBUFS, ARP to the ISP gateway incomplete), so even though the modem re-registered as OPERATIONAL after its ~02:02 reboot, no traffic passes; four WAN reloads (rc=0) could not clear the hung driver.
evidence: dmesg -a: multiple 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' entries interleaved with 'link state changed to DOWN/UP' — the interface flapped (matching the watchdog reloads) but the queue timeouts kept recurring
netstat -i: vtnet0 shows Oerrs=48211 while vtnet1 has 0 errors — damage is confined to the WAN NIC
ping -c 3 198.51.100.1 (ISP gateway): 'sendto: No buffer space available', 100% loss — sends fail at the stuck NIC, not downstream
arp -n: entry for default gateway 198.51.100.1 '(incomplete)' while LAN neighbors resolve normally — L2 resolution through vtnet0 fails despite carrier being up
cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: reloads at 02:30, 02:40, 02:55, 03:25 all rc=0 yet outage continued; at 03:30 decision 'none' due to reload_cap (12/24h), so the watchdog can no longer act

cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl and modem-metrics.jsonl: modem rebooted ~02:02 ('Cable Modem Reboot... registration complete') and reports OPERATIONAL with healthy SNR since — provider side recovered, so it cannot explain the continuing outage
netstat -rn: default route via 198.51.100.1 on vtnet0 present and correct; ifconfig shows vtnet0 UP/RUNNING/LOWER_UP with lease 198.51.100.27 — routing and addressing are fine
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall to reset the hung vtnet0 NIC/driver; an interface reload has already been shown not to clear it. The modem_reboot is unnecessary (modem is registered and OPERATIONAL). Longer term, consider hardware review of the virtio WAN device or a watchdog escalation path that reboots the host when repeated reloads fail.
data.detail: WAN NIC (vtnet0) transmit queues hung; driver never recovers after link flaps
